newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh evacuates coast as cyclone nears.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh evacuates coast as cyclone nears.

text.p: A cyclone heading from the Bay of Bengal was only 250 kilometres (155 miles) from the Bangladesh coast early on Monday, threatening to slam onshore in next few hours, weather officials said.
The cyclone with wind speeds of 200 kph (112 mph) could trigger tidal surges up to five metres (16 feet), inundating widespread areas.
Over 33,000 Red Crescent and other volunteers have evacuated about half a million people to cyclone shelters and the process was continuing, officials said.
Over 131,000 people were moved to shelters in Cox's Bazar district alone, local administrator Ali Imam Majumder told Reuters.
Weather officials at Cox's Bazar said the cyclone had not changed its course but had been stationary for about three hours after Sunday midnight, which delayed its landfall.
"Now it's moving again and may hit the coast and offshore islands by midday," one official said.
Other meteorology department officials said they were expecting the cyclone to lose intensity if it did not lash the coast before Monday afternoon.
"This is the best we can hope at the moment," one official said.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina cancelled a planned trip to Spain on Sunday night. The authorities have put army, navy and other security officials on high alert for emergency rescue and relief operations.
Airforce planes from Chittagong base were moved to Dhaka while the navy sent its vessels to safety.
Fishermen have been warned not to leave port and coastal officials had been told to hoist "great danger" signals.
A total of 35 ships berthed at Chittagong and Mongla ports were moved to outer anchorages, port officials said.
"We are taking this precaution so the ships do not collide during the storm and jam the channel by sinking," said Chittagong Port Harbourmaster Quamrul Islam.
State-run radio and television broadcast frequent storm warnings.
People fleeing their homes or being moved to cyclone shelters have been asked to keep drinking water, food and other essentials underground to help them after the cyclone.
Bangladesh's worst cyclone in 1991 killed at least 138,000 people and left millions homeless.
